Let b be the speed in still water and c the speed of the current, over a fixed distance d. Downstream time is d/(b + c) and upstream time is d/(b - c); the condition that downstream takes half the upstream time gives 1/(b + c) = (1/2) x 1/(b - c), so 2(b - c) = b + c, i.e. b = 3c. The required ratio of still-water speed to current is therefore 3 : 1.
